        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e4dd748dc87cf431af7b3954963be0d9f6150217 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2022 13:44:21 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: fsl_sai: Fix FSL_SAI_xDR/xFR definition

There are multiple xDR and xFR registers, the index is
from 0 to 7. FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR is abandoned,
replace them with FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0.

Fixes: 4f7a0728b530 ("ASoC: fsl_sai: Add support for SAI new version")
Signed-off-by: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1653284661-18964-1-git-send-email-shengjiu.wang@nxp.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
---
 sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
index e4965efe6102..1c8f5ca07f9d 100644
--- a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
+++ b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
@@ -80,8 +80,8 @@
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR3(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR3(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR3(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR4(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR4(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR4(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR5(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR5(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR5(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
+#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
+#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
 #define FSL_SAI_xMR(tx)		(tx ? FSL_SAI_TMR : FSL_SAI_RMR)
 
 /* SAI Transmit/Receive Control Register */
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect definition of the FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR registers, which did not account for the multiple instances of these registers (indexed from 0 to 7). The original definitions were ambiguous and could lead to incorrect register access, as they did not specify which instance of the register was being referenced. The patch corrects this by replacing the generic definitions with specific ones for the first instance (FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0), ensuring that the correct registers are accessed in the code.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect definition of the FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR registers, which did not account for the multiple instances of these registers (indexed from 0 to 7). The original definitions were ambiguous and could lead to incorrect register access, as they did not specify which instance of the register was being referenced. The patch corrects this by replacing the generic definitions with specific ones for the first instance (FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0), ensuring that the correct registers are accessed in the code.
